Józsefváros (8. kerület) — Budapest, Hungary

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Historically one of Budapest's most discussed districts for public safety, and named in the July 2025 citywide theft-hotspot map. The picture here is genuinely mixed rather than one-directional: registered crime stayed roughly stable in 2025 (4,047 cases) versus 2024's five-year peak (4,234), and a permanent police presence installed at Blaha Lujza Square helped cut assault cases nearly in half (192 to 132) — but residential burglaries rose about 50% in the first quarter of 2025 (19 cases versus 13 a year earlier), and residents report ongoing problems with homeless people and drug users occupying stairwells ("drogosok beslisszolnak az ajtón"). The district's case-resolution rate for serious crime (56%) is the best of the five inner districts compared in a 2023 study, but its overall case-clearance rate has fallen from near 70% in 2021 to about 55% by 2025. Sources checked: Jozsefvarosujsag.hu, 10 Jul 2023 / updated 23 Feb 2024 (five-district crime-density comparison); Metropol.hu, 12 May 2025 (Q1 2025 burglary surge, resident complaints); Jozsefvarosujsag.hu, 2025 (five-year public-safety review, Blaha Lujza Square police presence); Metropol.hu, 20 Jul 2025 (30-day crime-hotspot map).
